reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, wide-packet re-review batch 1, 2026-08-01

samples_reviewed.question_text: The number 28 is written in words as 'eighteen'. True or False?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency requires both reading and writing numerals, but across all seven seeds -- including the widened true_false item at seed 50 ('The number 28 is written in words as 'eighteen'. True or False?') and the seed 72 cloze repeat of 'Write 15 in words.' -- every task converts a numeral to its word form; none asks a student to write the numeral given only its word form.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Adding formatters (true_false at seed 50, cloze at seed 72) still only rewraps the numeral-to-word direction; the reverse sub-case named by 'write numerals' -- producing digits from a dictated or worded number -- never appears in any of the seven widened samples.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Stems such as seed 43's 'Write 14 in words.' and seed 50's true/false sentence are short, single-clause, and use only number-word vocabulary appropriate for Grade 1 Quarter 1 readers.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three response formats now appear (mcq, true_false, cloze) but they all wrap the identical underlying task of naming a numeral's word form; seed 72's cloze repeats seed 46's exact stem 'Write 15 in words.' with only the answer format changed.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every rendered variation, from the mcq numeral prompts to the seed 50 true/false verification of '28... eighteen', stays on the read/write-numerals topic without drifting into an unrelated skill like comparison or counting.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The seven sampled numerals are 33, 14, 26, 21, 15, 28 and 15 again -- none exceeds 33, so almost none of the competency's stated up-to-100 range beyond the thirties is ever exercised.
